entities.name: Query Ham1p-like protein
observations: A 203-residue acidic protein (predicted pI 4.88; molecular mass about 22.1 kDa) contains a Ham1p-like domain spanning residues 6–199.
Shows 57.8–58.3% identity over about 98% of its length to curated bacterial dITP/XTP pyrophosphatases.
Likely cytosolic and probably functions as a homodimer by analogy to close curated homologs; these properties are homology-based, not directly experimentally established for the query.

entities.name: dITP/XTP pyrophosphatase
observations: Curated bacterial homologs are Mg2+-dependent pyrophosphatases that hydrolyze dITP, ITP, and XTP to the corresponding monophosphates plus diphosphate.
Annotated biological role is nucleotide-pool sanitization, preventing incorporation of noncanonical purines into DNA or RNA.
Representative curated homologs have EC 3.6.1.66 and are annotated as cytosolic homodimers.

entities.name: Purine nucleotide pool sanitization
observations: The inferred process removes damaged or noncanonical purine triphosphates from the nucleotide pool, reducing potential chromosomal lesions and aberrant nucleic-acid incorporation.
